title: Kotopoulo Kapama
subtitle: Greek chicken braised with tomato and cinnamon
excerpt: Chicken thighs simmered slowly in a spiced tomato sauce with cinnamon and cloves. Rich and deeply aromatic, served over pasta or rice to catch the sauce.
sourceNotes: Traditional Greek braised chicken dish; the cinnamon-spiced tomato sauce is common across mainland Greece and Cyprus.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the cooked chicken and sauce together for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently on the hob.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the quantity easily in a wide casserole. Use two pans if needed to brown the chicken in a single layer.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes better the next day. Make fully, cool, refrigerate, and reheat gently before serving.

content.text: Kapama is a braised dish built on a spiced tomato sauce with cinnamon at its centre. The chicken should be browned properly before the liquid goes in. A pale, steamed result misses the depth the dish needs.
Pat the chicken dry and season well with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in the dutch oven over a medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken, skin side down, for 5 to 6 minutes until deep golden. Turn and brown the other side for 3 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Pour off most of the fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon. Add the onion and cook over a medium heat for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, cinnamon stick, cloves, and bay leaves. Stir for 1 minute. Add the tomato puree and stir for another minute.
Pour in the wine if using and let it bubble for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes and stock. Stir and bring to a simmer.
Return the chicken to the pot, skin side up. Cover with the lid slightly ajar and simmer on a low heat for 45 minutes.
Remove the cinnamon stick, cloves, and bay leaves. Rest for 5 minutes before serving over pasta or rice.

items.symptom: The sauce is thin and watery.
items.cause: The lid was on too tightly, or the heat was too low to reduce the liquid.
items.fix: Remove the lid fully for the last 15 minutes and turn the heat up slightly. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

items.symptom: The chicken skin is soft rather than coloured.
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough before the chicken went in, or the pan was overcrowded.
items.fix: Pat the chicken dry before browning and use a pan large enough to hold the pieces without touching.

items.cause: The whole spices were left in too long.
items.fix: Remove the cinnamon, cloves, and bay leaves after 30 minutes of simmering if the flavour is strong enough.
